newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin wants to boost secondary bond trade.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin wants to boost secondary bond trade.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry is discussing with the bourse, brokerages, the central bank and the National Securities Depository ways of boosting secondary interbank T-bond trade in 1997, a ministry official said.
Piotr Dziewulski, head of the public debt department, told a news conference higher liquidity in secondary bond trade was one of the ministry's top goals for next year.
"Higher liquidity on the secondary bond market is likely to boost demand for the papers and allow lower transaction costs," Dziewulski said.
"We are in talks with the bourse, the central bank, the National Securities Depository (KDPW) and securities houses on how to make secondary bond trade more liquid," he said.
"This might require some legal changes, but it is too early to be more precise," he added.
Dealers say current rules on secondary bond trade pose problems for dealers where settlement is concerned, which, though not insurmountable, do hamper trade.
Dealers estimate average daily turnover on the secondary bond market over the last six months at between 10-20 million zlotys compared with some two billion in secondary T-bill trade.

"To improve bond trade the four existing secondary bond markets -- interbank, bourse block and public as well as the over-the-counter -- should become one and many formalities should be scrapped," one dealer said.
To improve bond trade liquidity the finance ministry also plans to a publish a quarterly diary of its treasury paper auctions, for both T-bills and bonds.
"We want our borrowing needs to be as predictable as possible, because this helps investors build their portfolios," Dziewulski said.
He said it was impossible to determine when any concrete decisions on improving secondary market trade could be made.
